title: Pediatric TB specimens
dek: Children are paucibacillary, swallow sputum, and rarely cavity. Stool and nasopharyngeal WRDs exist because gastric aspirates do not scale.
story: Childhood TB is a diagnostic insult: low bacillary load, often no cavity, often no productive cough. Expectation of a 3+ smear is how programmes miss kids. Clinical scores plus mWRDs plus (when you can) culture are the spine; IGRA/TST can support infection but do not prove disease.

Specimen menu: induced sputum, nasopharyngeal aspirate, gastric aspirate (swallowed overnight sputum), stool for Xpert Ultra (WHO-endorsed), lymph-node FNA, CSF in meningitis. Stool is not a joke specimen — it is a logistics solution that detects swallowed MTBC DNA/bacilli.
A negative WRD never rules out pediatric TB. Treat on clinical grounds when the alternative is watching miliary disease bloom. That is WHO, not cowboy medicine — document the algorithm.
deepTitle: What Ultra trace means in a toddler
deep: Unlike a previously treated adult lung, a treatment-naive child with trace Ultra is a much higher-stakes true-positive prior. Context is the whole assay.
Gastric aspirate pH and delay kill culture. WRDs are more forgiving of dead bacilli, which is a feature and a bug.
Household-source investigation is part of diagnosis: the child’s “lab” is often the adult’s sputum.
LF-LAM has a pediatric/HIV story but is not a universal child screen.

visual.caption: Specimen choices when the child cannot spit. Sensitivity is generally stool/NPA/induced sputum in the WRD era; culture remains the viability backstop. Clinical diagnosis sits above a negative lab.

example.title: Stool Ultra positive, gastric culture negative
example.setup: 18-month-old contact of a 3+ index. Stool Ultra MTB detected, RIF not detected. Gastric aspirate culture negative. CXR: hilar adenopathy.

steps.title: Do not discard the WRD
steps.body: Culture miss on gastric samples is common. Clinical plus NAAT is a disease diagnosis.

steps.title: RIF-not-detected is a window, not a full DST
steps.body: If the source is RR-TB, the child’s RIF result still needs a second thought and better sampling.

steps.title: Treat as DS-TB unless the source says otherwise
steps.body: Pediatric regimens (including SHINE 4-month for non-severe) follow disease severity, not the stool brand name.

example.takeaway: Kids need a specimen strategy, not adult smear expectations.

check.prompt: Stool as an Xpert Ultra specimen in children works because:
choices: Children swallow respiratory secretions; WRDs can detect MTBC DNA/bacilli in stool
check.answer: Children swallow respiratory secretions; WRDs can detect MTBC DNA/bacilli in stool
check.why: Logistics plus swallowed sputum, not a GI-tropism claim.

choices: Be declared not TB because WRDs are 100% sensitive in children
